source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: Elucidatio capituli primi: Onus Ninive, liber visionis Nahum.
1.title_en: Explanation of the first chapter: The burden of Ninive, the book of the vision of Nahum.

paras.t: Nahum propheta, decem tribubus jam ab Assyriis captis, regnante Ezechia super Judam, legitur prophetasse. Describit autem destructionem Ninive metropolis Assyriorum, contra quam vaticinatus est Jonas. Quum enim ad prædicationem Jonæ Ninivitæ ad tempus pœnituissent, post aliquantum temporis ad vomitum redierunt. Idcirco per Nahum prædicit eos Spiritus Sanctus perituros.
paras.en: Nahum the prophet is read to have prophesied when the ten tribes had already been taken captive by the Assyrians, while Ezechias reigned over Juda. He describes the destruction of Ninive, the capital city of the Assyrians, against which Jonas prophesied[[Jon 3:1||]]. For although the Ninivites had done penance for a time at the preaching of Jonas, after a while they returned to their vomit. Therefore the Holy Ghost foretells through Nahum that they will perish.

paras.t: Onus Ninive, id est pondus miseriæ, seu gravis calamitas Assyriorum, est liber, id est materia libri, visionis Nahum Elcesæi, id est nati de loco sic dicto: qui fuit viculus Galilææ tempore Hieronymi pene destructus, quem refert sibi Hieronymus a circumducente monstratum. Ex quo constat, quod Elcesæi non est hic nomen proprium viri, et patris Nahum, sed nomen loci natalis.
paras.en: [[1:1|The burden of Ninive|Onus Ninive]], that is, the weight of misery, or the heavy calamity of the Assyrians, is the [[1:1|book|liber]], that is, the matter of the book, [[1:1|of the vision of Nahum, the Elcesite|visionis Nahum Elcesæi]], that is, of one born in the place so called: this was a little village of Galilee, almost destroyed in the time of Jerome, who relates that it was shown to him by the man who was guiding him about. From this it is plain that *Elcesite* is not here the proper name of a man, the father of Nahum, but the name of his birthplace.

paras.t: Deus æmulator, id est zelator et ultionis amator secundum zelum justitiæ suæ. Eadem verba Moyses scripsit. Et in Exodo Dominus protestatur: Ego Dominus fortis, zelotes. Est autem zelus alius quidem spiritualis et bonus, alius carnalis et vitiosus. De primo scriptum est, Zelus domus tuæ comedit me; de secundo, Noli æmulari in malignantibus, neque zelaveris facientes iniquitatem. Et ulciscens Dominus. Nullum enim malum dimittit impunitum, juxta illud, Deus inultum abire non patitur; et in Psalmo, Deus ultionum Dominus. Ipse quippe essentialiter sanctus et justus est, ideo omne peccatum detestatur, ac punit in hoc sæculo vel futuro. Punit autem in his qui convertuntur ac pœnitent, dum illi Deo inspirante castigant se ipsos. Ulciscens Dominus et habens furorem, id est summum æquitatis rigorem, seu justitiam tam districte vindicantem, ac si furiosus consisteret Dominus. Quod autem Deus in sua natura non habeat passionem, seu sensitivæ partis aliquam affectionem, certissimum est. Ulciscens Dominus, injuriam sibi illatam vindicando, in hostes suos, id est obduratos et infideles, qui odiunt Deum, et odio habentur ab eo, et irascens ipse inimicis suis, id est, per modum irati se habentes in puniendo rebelles.
paras.en: [[1:2|The Lord is a jealous God|Deus æmulator]], that is, zealous, and a lover of vengeance according to the zeal of his justice. Moses wrote the same words[[Ex 34:14||]][[Deut 4:24||]][[Deut 5:9||]][[Deut 6:15||]]. And in Exodus the Lord declares: [[Ex 20:5|I am the Lord thy God, mighty, jealous|Ego Dominus fortis, zelotes]]. Now there is one zeal that is spiritual and good, another that is carnal and vicious. Of the first it is written: [[Ps 68:10|the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up|Zelus domus tuæ comedit me]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxviii, 10; the words are Ps 68:10]; of the second: [[Ps 36:1|Be not emulous of evildoers; nor envy them that work iniquity|Noli æmulari in malignantibus, neque zelaveris facientes iniquitatem]]. [[1:2|and a revenger|Et ulciscens Dominus]]. For he lets no evil go unpunished, according to that saying: [[Job 24:12|God doth not suffer it to pass unrevenged|Deus inultum abire non patitur]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 93:1|The Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth|Deus ultionum Dominus]]. For he is in his very essence holy and just; therefore he detests every sin, and punishes it in this world or in the world to come. And he punishes it in those who are converted and do penance, when they, at God's inspiring, chastise themselves. [[1:2|the Lord is a revenger, and hath wrath|Ulciscens Dominus et habens furorem]], that is, the utmost rigour of equity, or a justice that avenges so strictly that it is as though the Lord were in a fury [the Latin *furor* is rage or madness; hence Denis's caution that follows]. But that God in his nature has no passion, nor any affection of the sensitive part [that is, of the lower powers of the soul, which feel through the body], is most certain. [[1:2|the Lord taketh vengeance|Ulciscens Dominus]], avenging the wrong done to him, [[1:2|on his adversaries|in hostes suos]], that is, the hardened and unbelieving, who hate God and are hated by him, [[1:2|and he is angry with his enemies|et irascens ipse inimicis suis]], that is, bearing himself like one who is angry in punishing the rebellious.

paras.t: Hæc præmisit Propheta, eo quod Assyriorum punitionem scripturus sit. Sed quia punitio Dei ad patientium utilitatem ordinatur, nec statim infertur, sed diu et clementer differtur, adjicit: Dominus patiens, id est, longanimiter præstolans errantium pœnitentiam. Si autem patientia proprie accipiatur, prout est virtus moralis passionem tristitiæ ordinans, sic non competit Deo proprie, sed metaphorice, quemadmodum cæteræ passiones et virtutes passionum refrenatrices. Et magnus fortitudine, imo infinitæ virtutis, et ipsa divina essentia est potestas omnipotens atque immensa. Unde in libro Job habetur: Ecce, Deus excelsus in fortitudine sua, et nullus similis ei in legislatoribus. Jeremias quoque ait: Magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine. Quis non timebit te, o Rex gentium? Et mundans per gratiam impium seu nocentem, non faciet innocentem, id est, non permittet eum sine debita pœna evadere. Vel, Mundans immundum (quis enim potest facere mundum de immundo conceptum semine? nonne solus Deus?) non faciet innocentem, id est a correctione liberum, sed flagellabit omnem quem recipit filium. Propter quod ait per Jeremiam: Castigabo te in judicio, ut non tibi videaris innoxius.
paras.en: The prophet set these things first because he is about to write of the punishment of the Assyrians. But since God's punishment is ordered to the profit of those who suffer it, and is not inflicted at once but long and mercifully deferred, he adds: [[1:3|The Lord is patient|Dominus patiens]], that is, waiting with long-suffering for the repentance of those who go astray. But if patience is taken in its proper sense, as the moral virtue that governs the passion of sorrow, then it does not belong to God properly but metaphorically, like the other passions and the virtues that rein in the passions. [[1:3|and great in power|Et magnus fortitudine]], nay, of infinite might; and the divine essence itself is power almighty and immeasurable. Hence it is found in the book of Job: [[Job 36:22|Behold, God is high in his strength, and none is like him among the lawgivers|Ecce, Deus excelsus in fortitudine sua, et nullus similis ei in legislatoribus]]. Jeremias also says: [[Jer 10:6|thou art great, and great is thy name in might|Magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine]]. [[Jer 10:7|Who shall not fear thee, O king of nations?|Quis non timebit te, o Rex gentium?]] [[1:3|and will not cleanse|Et mundans]] [the Latin *et mundans non faciet innocentem* says word for word "and cleansing, he will not make innocent", and Denis expounds it in that sense], that is, cleansing by grace the wicked or guilty man, [[1:3|and acquit the guilty|non faciet innocentem]], that is, he will not let him escape without due punishment. Or: cleansing the unclean (for [[Job 14:4|Who can make him clean that is conceived of unclean seed?|quis enim potest facere mundum de immundo conceptum semine?]] Is it not God alone?), he will not make him innocent, that is, free from correction, but [[Heb 12:6|he scourgeth every son whom he receiveth|flagellabit omnem quem recipit filium]]. For this reason he says through Jeremias: [[Jer 30:11|I will chastise thee in judgment, that thou mayst not seem to thyself innocent|Castigabo te in judicio, ut non tibi videaris innoxius]].

paras.t: Dominus in tempestate et in turbine viæ ejus. Per vias Domini, hoc loco intelligit operationes divinæ justitiæ contra iniquos, videlicet ultiones ex divina justitia procedentes: quæ dicuntur esse in tempestate et turbine, quoniam impetuose nonnunquam horribiliterque infliguntur; et interdum ipsa tempestas aeris, et turbo ventorum, fulgura atque tonitrua, sunt effectus ultricis justitiæ Dei, quemadmodum factum esse contra Ægyptios patet in Exodo. Hinc Jeremias ait: Ecce turbo dominicæ indignationis egredietur, et tempestas erumpens super caput impiorum veniet. Et nebulæ, scilicet sunt, pulvis pedum ejus: id est, accessus Dei vindicantis ad impios ita terribilis est, ut nebulæ appellentur pulvis pedum ejus, quoniam obscura et tristia sunt omnia quæ infligit. Non quod Deus in sua natura habeat pedes, sed pedes Dei dicuntur potestas qua venit et calcat iniquos. Vel ideo pulvis pedum Dei dicitur nebula, quia ex tempestate et turbine causatis a Deo, multum de pulvere ascendit in aerem, quem per modum nebulæ obscurat ac implet. Et dicitur pulvis pedum Dei, quia a terra elevatur, quæ fertur scabellum pedum Dei. Unde in Isaia ait: Cœlum mihi sedes est, terra autem scabellum pedum meorum.
paras.en: [[1:3|The Lord's ways are in a tempest, and a whirlwind|Dominus in tempestate et in turbine viæ ejus]]. By the ways of the Lord he here understands the works of divine justice against the wicked, namely the punishments that proceed from divine justice; and these are said to be in a tempest and a whirlwind because they are sometimes inflicted violently and dreadfully. And sometimes the very tempest of the air and the whirlwind of the winds, the lightnings and thunders, are effects of God's avenging justice, as is plain in Exodus, where this was done against the Egyptians[[Ex 9:23||]]. Hence Jeremias says: [[Jer 23:19|Behold the whirlwind of the Lord's indignation shall come forth, and a tempest shall break out and come upon the head of the wicked|Ecce turbo dominicæ indignationis egredietur, et tempestas erumpens super caput impiorum veniet]]. [[1:3|and clouds|Et nebulæ]] (understand: *are*) [[1:3|the dust of his feet|pulvis pedum ejus]]: that is, the approach of God when he comes to take vengeance on the wicked is so terrible that clouds are called the dust of his feet, because all that he inflicts is dark and grievous. Not that God in his nature has feet; but the power by which he comes and treads down the wicked is called the feet of God. Or else the cloud is called the dust of God's feet because, through the tempest and whirlwind caused by God, much dust rises into the air, and darkens and fills it in the manner of a cloud. And it is called the dust of God's feet because it is raised from the earth, which is said to be the footstool of God's feet. Hence he says in Isaias: [[Is 66:1|Heaven is my throne, and the earth my footstool|Cœlum mihi sedes est, terra autem scabellum pedum meorum]].

paras.t: Increpans mare, id est, aquis universis per modum redarguentis præcipiens: quemadmodum Christus fecit orta tempestate in mari, juxta illud Marci: Surgens Jesus comminatus est vento, et dixit mari, Tace et obmutesce. Non tamen opinandum est elementa mundi esse animata ac viva, ut Dei increpationem agnoscant; nec ponenda est anima mundi, quemadmodum Plato asseruit totum mundum esse unum animal divina sanctione intelligens. Et exsiccans illud. Non quod aqua fiat sicca, quum humiditas sit inseparabilis qualitas aquæ, sed quod terra seu alveus maris siccetur. Sic enim Deus dicitur mare Rubrum ac Jordanem siccasse, juxta illud in Psalmo: Increpuit mare Rubrum, et exsiccatum est. Et omnia flumina ad desertum deducens, quum sibi placuerit. Potest enim aquas trans ripas educere.
paras.en: [[1:4|He rebuketh the sea|Increpans mare]], that is, commanding all the waters in the manner of one who reproves: as Christ did when a storm arose on the sea, according to that of Mark: Jesus, [[Mark 4:39|rising up, he rebuked the wind, and said to the sea: Peace, be still|Surgens Jesus comminatus est vento, et dixit mari, Tace et obmutesce]]. Yet it is not to be supposed that the elements of the world are animate and living, so as to perceive God's rebuke; nor is a soul of the world to be posited, as Plato asserted that the whole world is one living being, endowed with understanding by divine decree. [[1:4|and drieth it up|Et exsiccans illud]]: not that the water becomes dry, since moisture is a quality inseparable from water, but that the ground or bed of the sea is dried. For in this way God is said to have dried up the Red Sea and the Jordan, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 105:9|he rebuked the Red Sea and it was dried up|Increpuit mare Rubrum, et exsiccatum est]]. [[1:4|and bringeth all the rivers to be a desert|Et omnia flumina ad desertum deducens]], when it pleases him. For he can lead the waters out beyond their banks.

paras.t: In præinductis verbis laudavit Propheta divinam justitiam, misericordiam, et potestatem.
paras.en: In the words set down so far the prophet has praised God's justice, mercy and power.

paras.t: Infirmatus est Basan et Carmelus, et flos Libani elanguit. Basan fuit in terra promissionis regio uberrima; Carmelus vero et Libanus, montes arboribus consiti et fecundi atque pulcherrimi. Per quæ, secundum Hieronymum, Propheta metaphorice exprimit vastitatem Assyriorum a Chaldæis: ut per Basan intelligatur fertilis terra Assur; per Carmelum, exercitus Assyriorum; per florem Libani, rex et principes. Alii exponunt de prædictis locis filiorum Israel: quæ dicuntur infirmata propter sterilitatem et caristiam quæ contigit in terra Israel tempore Eliæ et Elisei, ut patet tertio et quarto libris Regum; sicque flos Libani elanguit, id est, florida germina defecerunt.
paras.en: [[1:4|Basan languisheth and Carmel: and the flower of Libanus fadeth away|Infirmatus est Basan et Carmelus, et flos Libani elanguit]]. Basan was a most fruitful region in the land of promise, and Carmel and Libanus are mountains planted with trees, fruitful and very beautiful. By these, according to Jerome, the prophet expresses figuratively the laying waste of the Assyrians by the Chaldeans: so that by Basan is understood the fertile land of Assur; by Carmel, the army of the Assyrians; by the flower of Libanus, the king and the princes. Others expound it of the places just named in the land of the children of Israel, which are said to languish because of the barrenness and dearth that befell the land of Israel in the time of Elias and Eliseus, as is plain in the third and fourth books of Kings[[3 Kings 18:2||]][[4 Kings 6:25||]]; and so [[1:4|the flower of Libanus fadeth away|flos Libani elanguit]], that is, the flowering shoots failed.

paras.t: Montes commoti sunt ab eo, et colles desolati sunt. Hoc accipi potest de materialibus montibus terræ et collibus, qui frequenter divina virtute moventur et dejiciuntur; vel de superioribus et inferioribus principibus, qui Deo vindicante turbantur, desolantur, et a sua gloria transmutantur. Possunt demum omnia hæc specialiter ad Assyrios et Niniven retorqueri, quum in principio capituli dictum sit, Onus Ninive. Et contremuit terra a facie ejus, id est a divinæ virtutis imperio seu adspectu, qui respicit terram, et facit eam tremere, et orbis et omnes habitantes in eo. Omnia ista frequenter ad litteram acciderunt, vel simul, vel per partes. In diluvio namque simpliciter totus orbis cum habitatoribus suis commotus est, seu multipliciter immutatus.
paras.en: [[1:5|The mountains tremble at him, and the hills are made desolate|Montes commoti sunt ab eo, et colles desolati sunt]]. This can be taken of the material mountains and hills of the earth, which are often moved and cast down by divine power; or of princes higher and lower, who, when God takes vengeance, are troubled, made desolate and fallen from their glory. Lastly, all these things can be turned specially to the Assyrians and Ninive, since at the beginning of the chapter it was said: [[1:1|The burden of Ninive|Onus Ninive]]. [[1:5|and the earth hath quaked at his presence|Et contremuit terra a facie ejus]], that is, at the command or the gaze of the divine power, which [[Ps 103:32|looketh upon the earth, and maketh it tremble|qui respicit terram, et facit eam tremere]], [[1:5|and the world, and all that dwell therein|et orbis et omnes habitantes in eo]]. All these things have often happened to the letter, either together or in part. For in the Flood the whole world with its inhabitants was utterly shaken, or changed in many ways[[Gen 7:11||]].

paras.t: Ante faciem indignationis ejus quis stabit? id est, præsentiam divinæ ultionis ferre quis poterit, quum et in Psalmo dicatur: Ante faciem frigoris ejus quis sustinebit? Et per Jeremiam Dominus loquitur: Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me? et quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo? Ideo subditur: Et quis resistet in ira furoris ejus? id est, rigori justitiæ atque vindictæ omnipotentis Dei quis se opponet, reluctabitur, prævalebit? Palam quod nullus, nisi in quantum ipsemet Deus voluerit, secundum quod Moyses Deum iratum placavit, inæstimabili magnitudine caritatis quodammodo prævalens. Unde in Job inducitur: Deus, cujus iræ nemo resistere potest, sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem. Indignatio ejus effusa est ut ignis, id est, ultio Dei vitia detestantis, desævit in impiis dure et horribiliter nimis, et petræ dissolutæ sunt ab eo, id est, lapidea corda resoluta sunt, victa et emollita. Frequenter enim Deus exercuit in veteri Testamento, tam in populo suo quam gentibus, hujusmodi ultionem. Præcipue tamen ut ignis effusa est indignatio Dei, quando super Pentapolim pluit ignem et sulfur. Ex vehementi quoque calore solent sæpe saxa resolvi.
paras.en: [[1:6|Who can stand before the face of his indignation?|Ante faciem indignationis ejus quis stabit?]] that is, who will be able to bear the presence of divine vengeance? For in the Psalm too it is said: [[Ps 147:6|who shall stand before the face of his cold?|Ante faciem frigoris ejus quis sustinebit?]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlvii, 17, the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate it is Ps 147:6]. And through Jeremias the Lord says: [[Jer 49:19|who is like to me? and who shall abide me? and who is that shepherd that can withstand my countenance?|Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me? et quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo?]] Therefore it is added: [[1:6|and who shall resist in the fierceness of his anger?|Et quis resistet in ira furoris ejus?]] that is, who will set himself against the rigour of the justice and vengeance of almighty God, struggle against it, prevail over it? Plainly no one, except in so far as God himself wills, in the way that Moses appeased God when he was angry[[Ex 32:11||]][[Ex 32:14||]], prevailing in a manner by the inestimable greatness of his charity. Hence in Job it is said: [[Job 9:13|God, whose wrath no man can resist, and under whom they stoop that bear up the world|Deus, cujus iræ nemo resistere potest, sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem]]. [[1:6|his indignation is poured out like fire|Indignatio ejus effusa est ut ignis]], that is, the vengeance of God, who detests vices, rages against the wicked harshly and exceedingly dreadfully, [[1:6|and the rocks are melted by him|et petræ dissolutæ sunt ab eo]], that is, stony hearts are dissolved, overcome and softened. For God often exercised vengeance of this kind in the Old Testament, both on his own people and on the Gentiles. But above all the indignation of God was poured out like fire when he rained fire and brimstone upon the Pentapolis [the five cities of the plain, Sodom and its neighbours]. And rocks are often wont to be dissolved by vehement heat.

paras.t: Bonus Dominus. Est enim naturaliter bonus, cujus natura est bonitas pura immensa, in tantum ut comparatione ejus nullus sit bonus, Christo testante apud Marcum: Nemo bonus, nisi unus Deus. Et confortans in die tribulationis: tunc enim promptissimus est ad miserendum, dummodo clamemus ad eum. Non enim patietur nos tentari supra id quod possumus. Et sciens per approbationem, sperantes in se. Novit enim Dominus qui sunt ejus. Istud litteraliter potest referri, quod tempore quo Assyrii tribulabant regnum Juda, Deus confortavit Ezechiam ac populum ejus sperantem in Deo; vel, quod tempore vastitatis Assyriorum a Chaldæis, confortavit ac liberavit sperantes in se Judæos commorantes inter Assyrios, ne simul cum illis trucidarentur a Chaldæis.
paras.en: [[1:7|The Lord is good|Bonus Dominus]]. For he is good by nature, his nature being pure and boundless goodness, so much so that in comparison with him no one is good, as Christ testifies in Mark: [[Mark 10:18|None is good but one, that is God|Nemo bonus, nisi unus Deus]]. [[1:7|and giveth strength in the day of trouble|Et confortans in die tribulationis]]: for then he is most ready to have mercy, provided we cry to him. For he [[1 Cor 10:13|will not suffer you to be tempted above that which you are able|patietur nos tentari supra id quod possumus]] [Denis has "us … we are able"]. [[1:7|and knoweth|Et sciens]] with approval [that is, with the knowledge by which God approves and owns his own, not bare knowing] [[1:7|them that hope in him|sperantes in se]]. For [[2 Tim 2:19|the Lord knoweth who are his|Novit enim Dominus qui sunt ejus]]. This can be referred literally to the time when the Assyrians were troubling the kingdom of Juda, and God strengthened Ezechias and his people, who hoped in God[[4 Kings 19:20||]]; or to the time when the Assyrians were laid waste by the Chaldeans, and he strengthened and delivered the Jews dwelling among the Assyrians who hoped in him, so that they should not be slaughtered by the Chaldeans together with them.

paras.t: Et in diluvio prætereunte, id est in exercitu Assyriorum, per modum diluvii super regnum Juda irruente, quemadmodum Isaias prædixit: Ibit per Judam inundans; consummationem faciet loci ejus, id est consummatam punitionem hujus diluvii, interficiendo per angelum in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia hominum. Et inimicos ejus, id est Assyrios, persequentur tenebræ tribulationis et mortis.
paras.en: [[1:8|But with a flood that passeth by|Et in diluvio prætereunte]], that is, in the army of the Assyrians rushing like a flood upon the kingdom of Juda, as Isaias foretold: He [[Is 8:8|shall pass through Juda, overflowing|Ibit per Judam inundans]]; [[1:8|he will make an utter end of the place thereof|consummationem faciet loci ejus]], that is, a full and final punishment of this flood, by slaying through the angel a hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the camp of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 19:35||]]. And [[1:8|his enemies|Et inimicos ejus]], that is, the Assyrians, [[1:8|darkness shall pursue|persequentur tenebræ]]: the darkness of tribulation and death.

paras.t: Quid cogitatis contra Dominum? id est, cur, o Assyrii, proponitis destruere regnum Juda et urbem ac templum Jerusalem, sicut destructum est decem tribuum regnum? Consummationem ipse faciet, id est, exercitum vestrum occidet; et non consurget duplex tribulatio, id est, Dominus non tradet regnum duarum tribuum in manus Sennacherib, quemadmodum tradidit regnum decem tribuum in manus Salmanasar patris Sennacherib. Porro de intellectu hujus verbi, post pauca plenius est dicendum.
paras.en: [[1:9|What do ye devise against the Lord?|Quid cogitatis contra Dominum?]] that is, why, O Assyrians, do you purpose to destroy the kingdom of Juda and the city and temple of Jerusalem, as the kingdom of the ten tribes was destroyed? [[1:9|he will make an utter end|Consummationem ipse faciet]], that is, he will slay your army; [[1:9|there shall not rise a double affliction|et non consurget duplex tribulatio]], that is, the Lord will not deliver the kingdom of the two tribes into the hands of Sennacherib, as he delivered the kingdom of the ten tribes into the hands of Salmanasar, the father of Sennacherib[[4 Kings 17:3||]][[4 Kings 17:6||]]. But more must be said a little later about the meaning of this saying.

paras.t: Quia sicut spinæ se invicem complectuntur, id est, adunantur, et quasi in fasciculum colligantur, ut pariter projiciantur in ignem; sic convivium eorum pariter potantium consumetur, id est, epulatio Assyriorum in terra Juda adhuc exsistentium et convivantium, mox cessabit, et in mœrorem vertetur, quasi stipula ariditate plena, id est valde velociter, quemadmodum siccissima stipula subito ab igne consumitur. Quum enim Sennacherib secundo redisset contra Judæam, et jam circa Jerusalem pernoctaret in Nobe, juxta illud in Isaia, Adhuc dies est, ut in Nobe stetur: de vespere fecit exercitui suo grande convivium, quasi de victoria certus; sed eadem nocte per angelum cæsus est populus ejus, et incinerata sunt corpora pessimorum.
paras.en: [[1:10|For as thorns embrace one another|Quia sicut spinæ se invicem complectuntur]], that is, are gathered together and bound up as it were into a bundle, so as to be thrown into the fire together; [[1:10|so while they are feasting and drinking together|sic convivium eorum pariter potantium]], [[1:10|they shall be consumed|consumetur]] [Denis reads *consumetur*, "the banquet … shall be consumed"], that is, the feasting of the Assyrians who are still in the land of Juda and banqueting there will soon cease and be turned into mourning, [[1:10|as stubble that is fully dry|quasi stipula ariditate plena]], that is, very swiftly, as the driest stubble is suddenly consumed by fire. For when Sennacherib had come back a second time against Judea, and was already spending the night near Jerusalem at Nobe, according to that in Isaias: [[Is 10:32|It is yet day enough, to remain in Nobe|Adhuc dies est, ut in Nobe stetur]], in the evening he made a great banquet for his army, as though sure of victory; but that same night his people were slain by the angel, and the bodies of those most wicked men were burnt to ashes.

paras.t: Ex te, id est ex populo tuo, o Sennacherib, exibit cogitans contra Dominum malitiam. Iste fuit Rabsaces, quem misit Sennacherib contra Jerusalem, quando Sennacherib exivit Judæam contra regem Æthiopiæ invadentem terram Assyriorum. Et sic in hac prophetia non servatur ordo historiæ, sicut nec frequenter in aliis locis Scripturæ. Rabsaces autem in via cogitavit quas blasphemias evomeret contra Deum Judæorum. Mente pertractans prævaricationem. Cogitavit enim qualiter posset Judæos terrere, et a spe divina avertere, sicque desperantes traderent se regi Assyriorum.
paras.en: [[1:11|Out of thee|Ex te]], that is, out of thy people, O Sennacherib, [[1:11|shall come forth one that imagineth evil against the Lord|exibit cogitans contra Dominum malitiam]]. This was Rabsaces, whom Sennacherib sent against Jerusalem[[Is 36:2||]][[4 Kings 18:17||]] when Sennacherib went out of Judea against the king of Ethiopia, who was invading the land of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 19:8||]][[4 Kings 19:9||]]. And so in this prophecy the order of the history is not kept, as it often is not in other places of Scripture either. Rabsaces, then, thought out on the way what blasphemies he would spew out against the God of the Jews. [[1:11|contriving treachery in his mind|Mente pertractans prævaricationem]]. For he considered how he might terrify the Jews and turn them from their hope in God, so that in despair they would give themselves up to the king of the Assyrians.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Si perfecti fuerint, id est, quamvis pugnatores Assyrii fuerint potestate perfecti, et ita plures, id est numero abundantes, sicut abundant virtute; sic quoque attondentur, id est, nihilo minus facillime per angelum delebuntur, quemadmodum per acutam novaculam pili raduntur. Sic ergo occisio Assyriorum vocatur attonsio, ad innuendum quam cito ac facile ab angelo occiderentur. Juxta quem modum loquitur de eadem re Isaias: In die illa radet Dominus in novacula acuta in rege Assyriorum caput et caudam et barbam universam. Et pertransibunt, id est, Assyrii deficient; qui vero ab angelo occisi non fuerint, fugient ad propria loca. Afflixi ego Dominus Deus te, o Ezechia et popule Juda, per Assyrios; et non affligam te ultra per Assyrios. Non enim promittitur Juda omnimoda securitas in futurum, sed pro tempore. De hoc multa leguntur in Isaia et libro quarto Regum.
paras.en: [[1:12|Thus saith the Lord: Though they were perfect|Hæc dicit Dominus: Si perfecti fuerint]], that is, although the Assyrian fighting men be perfect in power, [[1:12|and many of them so|et ita plures]], that is, abounding in number as they abound in strength, [[1:12|yet thus shall they be cut off|sic quoque attondentur]] [the Latin *attondentur* means "they shall be shorn"], that is, they will none the less be destroyed by the angel most easily, as hairs are shaved off with a sharp razor. So the slaying of the Assyrians is called a shearing, to suggest how quickly and easily they would be slain by the angel. In the same manner Isaias speaks of the same event: [[Is 7:20|In that day the Lord shall shave with a razor|In die illa radet Dominus in novacula]] that is sharp, [[Is 7:20|by the king of the Assyrians, the head|in rege Assyriorum caput]] and the tail, [[Is 7:20|and the whole beard|et barbam universam]] [Denis quotes freely: the Vulgate has "with a razor that is hired … the head and the hairs of the feet"]. [[1:12|and he shall pass|Et pertransibunt]] [Denis reads *pertransibunt*, "they shall pass"], that is, the Assyrians will fail, and those who have not been slain by the angel will flee to their own places. [[1:12|I have afflicted|Afflixi]], I the Lord God, [[1:12|thee|te]], O Ezechias and people of Juda, by means of the Assyrians; [[1:12|and I will afflict thee no more|et non affligam te ultra]] by the Assyrians. For Juda is not promised complete security for the future, but for the time being. Much is read of this in Isaias and in the fourth book of Kings[[Is 37:21||]][[4 Kings 19:20||]].

paras.t: Et nunc conteram virgam ejus de dorso tuo, id est, potestatem Sennacherib, et tribulationem quam tibi inflixit, destruam ac delebo, et vincula tua dirumpam, id est, vincula quæ tibi paravit, timorem quoque, obsidionem ac pressuram, quibus te circumvallavit et vinxit, ita quod egredi non valebas, tollam a te, ut libere pergas quo cupis.
paras.en: [[1:13|And now I will break in pieces his rod with which he struck thy back|Et nunc conteram virgam ejus de dorso tuo]] [the Latin has only "his rod from off thy back"], that is, the power of Sennacherib and the affliction he inflicted on thee I will destroy and blot out; [[1:13|and I will burst thy bonds asunder|et vincula tua dirumpam]], that is, the bonds he prepared for thee, and also the fear, the siege and the oppression with which he hemmed thee in and bound thee, so that thou couldst not go out, I will take away from thee, so that thou mayest go freely wherever thou wilt.

paras.t: Consequenter Propheta ait ad Sennacherib: Et præcipiet super te Dominus, id est, angelo jubebit ut exercitum tuum occidat; Prophetis quoque, ut mortem illorum et tuam dejectionem prænuntiat, ne fortuitu et absque ullo judice facta appareant, sed Deo prænuntiante cuncta agantur. Non seminabitur ex nomine tuo amplius, id est, ad tuum imperium non fiet de cetero seminatio terræ. Vel sensus est: Non seminabitur, id est, non fiet conceptus seu generatio ex te. Utriusque ratio est, quoniam statim quum reversus esset in Ninivèn, et in templo suo deum suum deprecaretur, a propriis occisus est filiis, ut patet in libro Regum et in Isaia. Porro in Tobia habetur, quod post dies quadraginta quinque a fuga sua a Judæa, vel certe a reditu suo in Niniven, sit occisus. De domo dei tui interficiam, sculptile et conflatile ponam ego Dominus sepulcrum tuum, id est, inter idola tua in templo dei tui interficieris; quia inhonoratus es, id est contemptus a populo tuo. Assyrii enim et Ninivitæ, audientes quod propter blasphemiam atque superbiam Sennacherib in Deum Israel, occisi essent eorum propinqui et nobiles in Judæa, odiosum habuerunt Sennacherib, ut aliqui dicunt: adjicientes, quod Sennacherib timens a plebe interfici, ingressus est fanum dei sui, deprecans auxilio idoli liberari, cui et promisit se oblaturum duos filios seniores: quo cognito, illi eum necabant.
paras.en: Next the prophet says to Sennacherib: [[1:14|And the Lord will give a commandment concerning thee|Et præcipiet super te Dominus]], that is, he will command the angel to slay thy army, and the prophets also to foretell their death and thy overthrow, so that these things should not seem to happen by chance and without any judge, but that all should be done with God foretelling it. [[1:14|that no more of thy name shall be sown|Non seminabitur ex nomine tuo amplius]], that is, at thy command there will be no more sowing of the land. Or the sense is: there shall not be sown, that is, there shall be no conceiving or begetting from thee. The reason for both is that as soon as he had returned to Ninive, and was praying to his god in his temple, he was slain by his own sons, as is plain in the book of Kings and in Isaias[[4 Kings 19:37||]][[Is 37:38||]]. Moreover it is found in Tobias that he was slain forty-five days after his flight from Judea, or at any rate after his return to Ninive[[Tob 1:24||]]. [[1:14|out of the house of thy God|De domo dei tui]] [[1:14|I will destroy|interficiam]] [the Latin *interficiam* is "I will slay", which Denis takes of Sennacherib]; [[1:14|the graven and molten thing|sculptile et conflatile]] [[1:14|I will make|ponam]], I the Lord, [[1:14|thy grave|sepulcrum tuum]], that is, thou shalt be slain among thy idols in the temple of thy god; [[1:14|for thou art disgraced|quia inhonoratus es]], that is, despised by thy own people. For the Assyrians and Ninivites, hearing that their kinsmen and nobles had been slain in Judea because of Sennacherib's blasphemy and pride against the God of Israel, held Sennacherib in hatred, as some say; and they add that Sennacherib, fearing to be killed by the common people, went into the temple of his god, praying to be delivered by the help of the idol, and promised to offer it his two elder sons; and when they learned of this, they killed him.

paras.t: Ecce super montes, id est in locis altis ac manifestis, erunt pedes evangelizantis, et, pro id est, annuntiantis pacem, id est nuntii referentis Ezechiæ ac populo ejus mortem Assyriorum et fugam Sennacherib; vel nuntiorum quos misit Ezechias per totum regnum suum ad divulgandum interitum Assyriorum, atque ad convocandum Judæos in Jerusalem ad agendum celebritatem paschalem et ad spolia detrahenda, itemque ad gratias Domino referendas. Unde subjungitur: Celebra, Juda, id est tu, rex Ezechia, ac subditi tui, festivitates tuas, id est dies paschalis solennitatis. Legitur autem secundo Paralipomenon, quod Judæi propter obsidionem Assyriorum non valebant primo mense celebrare Pascha, quod interim occisis et fugatis Assyriis fecerunt mense secundo. Et redde vota tua, id est, promissa Deo solve, quæ vovisti pro tua ab Assyriis liberatione; quia non adjiciet ultra ut pertranseat in te Belial, id est, Sennacherib sine jugo exsistens et prævaricator atque apostata (hoc enim interpretatur Belial) non addet amplius perambulare ac devastare terram tuam; universus interiit, id est, tam rex quam populus ejus perierunt. Loquebatur autem Nahum de futuro per modum præteriti, propter certitudinem prophetiæ.
paras.en: [[1:15|Behold upon the mountains|Ecce super montes]], that is, in high and open places, there will be [[1:15|the feet of him that bringeth good tidings|pedes evangelizantis]], [[1:15|and|et]] (put here for *that is*) [[1:15|that preacheth peace|annuntiantis pacem]]: that is, of the messenger bringing word to Ezechias and his people of the death of the Assyrians and the flight of Sennacherib; or of the messengers whom Ezechias sent through all his kingdom to make known the destruction of the Assyrians, and to call the Jews together to Jerusalem to keep the paschal solemnity, to strip the spoils, and also to give thanks to the Lord. Hence it is added: [[1:15|O Juda, keep|Celebra, Juda]], that is, thou, King Ezechias, and thy subjects, [[1:15|thy festivals|festivitates tuas]], that is, the days of the paschal solemnity. For it is read in the second book of Paralipomenon that the Jews could not keep the Pasch in the first month because of the siege of the Assyrians, and that, the Assyrians having meanwhile been slain and put to flight, they kept it in the second month[[2 Par 30:3||]][[2 Par 30:13||]] [the reason given there is that the priests were not sanctified and the people not yet gathered; the siege is Denis's own reading]. [[1:15|and pay thy vows|Et redde vota tua]], that is, discharge the promises to God that thou didst vow for thy deliverance from the Assyrians; [[1:15|for Belial shall no more pass through thee again|quia non adjiciet ultra ut pertranseat in te Belial]], that is, Sennacherib, who is without yoke, a transgressor and an apostate (for this is what Belial means), will not again go through thy land and lay it waste; [[1:15|he is utterly cut off|universus interiit]], that is, both the king and his people have perished. Now Nahum spoke of the future in the manner of the past, because of the certainty of the prophecy.

1.title: Expositio spiritualis ac mystica ejusdem capituli primi.
1.title_en: Spiritual and mystical exposition of the same first chapter.

paras.t: Onus Ninive. Quemadmodum dictum est super Jonam, per Niniven (quæ interpretatur speciosa) figuratur hic mundus, quo oculis carnis nihil speciosius intuemur, qui tamen quoad habitatores suos multis pressuris afficitur. Itaque, Onus Ninive, id est punitio mundi seu reproborum, de quibus ait Salvator discipulis : Si de mundo essetis, mundus quod suum erat diligeret; quia vero de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo, propterea odit vos mundus. Liber visionis, id est materia spiritualis considerationis, Nahum, id est consolatoris, videlicet Christi, vel cujuscumque veri Catholici qui ad consolationem electorum pœnas prædicat reproborum et sæculi consummationem, quæ sunt electis materia spiritualis lætitiæ, sicut ait Salvator : His fieri incipientibus, levate capita vestra, quia appropinquat redemptio vestra. Recte quoque interpretatio ista conveniebat huic sancto Prophetæ, qui non mediocriter consolabatur filios Israel, puta duodecim tribus, Assyriorum vastitatem prædicendo, qui jam decem tribus transtulerant, et duas obsederunt.
paras.en: [[1:1|The burden of Ninive|Onus Ninive]]. As was said on Jonas, by Ninive (which is interpreted *beautiful*) is figured this world, than which we behold nothing more beautiful with the eyes of the flesh, and which yet, as to its inhabitants, is afflicted with many distresses. And so: [[1:1|The burden of Ninive|Onus Ninive]], that is, the punishment of the world, or of the reprobate, of whom the Saviour says to the disciples: [[John 15:19|If you had been of the world, the world would love its own: but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you|Si de mundo essetis, mundus quod suum erat diligeret; quia vero de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo, propterea odit vos mundus]]. [[1:1|The book of the vision|Liber visionis]], that is, the matter of spiritual consideration, [[1:1|of Nahum|Nahum]], that is, of the comforter, namely of Christ, or of any true Catholic who, for the comfort of the elect, preaches the punishments of the reprobate and the consummation of the world, which are to the elect matter for spiritual joy; as the Saviour says: [[Luke 21:28|when these things begin to come to pass|His fieri incipientibus]], [[Luke 21:28|lift up your heads, because your redemption is at hand|levate capita vestra, quia appropinquat redemptio vestra]]. This interpretation also rightly fitted this holy Prophet, who gave no small comfort to the children of Israel, that is, to the twelve tribes, by foretelling the devastation of the Assyrians, who had already carried away ten tribes and had besieged the other two.

paras.t: Deus æmulator, et ulciscens Dominus. Quod in isto capitulo de rigore divinæ justitiæ contra Assyrios litteraliter dicitur, Hieronymus spiritualiter refert ad finem mundi judiciumque futurum in fine sæculi. Tunc enim præcipue videbitur Deus iratus et furens in reprobos, quos nunc patienter exspectat ad veniam. Unde in Isaia legitur : Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo, ardens furor ejus et gravis ad portandum.
paras.en: [[1:2|The Lord is a jealous God, and a revenger|Deus æmulator, et ulciscens Dominus]]. What is said in this chapter, in the literal sense, of the rigour of the divine justice against the Assyrians, Jerome refers in the spiritual sense to the end of the world and the judgment to come at the end of the age. For then above all will God be seen angry and raging against the reprobate, whom now he patiently awaits unto pardon. Hence we read in Isaias: [[Is 30:27|Behold the name of the Lord cometh from afar, his wrath burneth, and is heavy to bear|Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo, ardens furor ejus et gravis ad portandum]].

paras.t: Dominus in tempestate et turbine viæ ejus. Hoc est quod ait Psalmista : Ignis ante ipsum præcedet; item, Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet, et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida ; et iterum, Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus. Et nebulæ, id est peccatores vitiis obscurati, æternique Solis splendorem ab aliis, ut queunt, impedientes, erunt pulvis pedum ejus, id est, a Christo penitus conculcabuntur, et quasi in nihilum redigentur, ita quod omne spirituale esse gratiæ gratificantis amittent. Ideo scriptum est : Ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum; et, Tanquam vas figuli confringes eos. Isaias quoque ait : Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei.
paras.en: [[1:3|The Lord's ways are in a tempest, and a whirlwind|Dominus in tempestate et turbine viæ ejus]]. This is what the Psalmist says: [[Ps 96:3|A fire shall go before him|Ignis ante ipsum præcedet]]; and again: [[Ps 49:3|A fire shall burn before him: and a mighty tempest shall be round about him|Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet, et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida]]; and once more: [[Ps 96:2|Clouds and darkness are round about him|Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus]]. [[1:3|and clouds|Et nebulæ]], that is, sinners darkened by vices, who keep others, as far as they can, from the brightness of the eternal Sun, shall be [[1:3|the dust of his feet|pulvis pedum ejus]]: that is, they shall be utterly trodden down by Christ and as it were brought to nothing, so that they shall lose all the spiritual being of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratificans*: the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God]. Therefore it is written: [[Ps 109:1|I make thy enemies thy footstool|Ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum]]; and: Thou [[Ps 2:9|shalt break them in pieces like a potter's vessel|Tanquam vas figuli confringes eos]]. Isaias too says: [[Is 45:25|they shall come to him, and all that resist him shall be confounded|Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei]].

paras.t: Increpans mare, id est mundum vitiis amaricatum, et peccatores instabiles, de quibus scriptum est in Isaia, Impii quasi mare fervens, quod quiescere non potest; et exsiccans illud, id est, fluenta documentorum falsorum carnalesque fluxus exhauriens. Infirmatus est Basan, id est, omnis potestas peccatoris in fine mundi deficiet : qui vitiis plenus, intus inordinatus est atque confusus. Non enim implevit illud Apostoli : Omnia honeste et secundum ordinem fiant in vobis. Basan autem interpretatur confusio. Et Carmelus, id est literalis tantum et carnalis circumcisionis scientia præditus : quales sunt grossi Judæi, sequentes litteram occidentem, non spiritum vivificantem. Carmelus vero interpretatur scientia circumcisionis. Et flos Libani elanguit, id est, omnis viror, pulchritudo, decor atque prosperitas sæculi tabefiet. Libanus autem candidatio interpretatur : per quem hoc loco corda mundana, temporaliter florida, vel sanctitatem prætendentia, seque conficte foris ornantia, intelliguntur. De quibus cantatur : Quoniam tanquam fœnum velociter arescent, et sicut olera herbarum cito decident. Unde in libro Sapientiæ fatentur : Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis? Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra præteriens; et nos nati, continuo desivimus esse.
paras.en: [[1:4|He rebuketh the sea|Increpans mare]], that is, the world made bitter by vices, and unstable sinners, of whom it is written in Isaias: [[Is 57:20|the wicked are like the raging sea, which cannot rest|Impii quasi mare fervens, quod quiescere non potest]]; [[1:4|and drieth it up|et exsiccans illud]], that is, draining the streams of false teachings and the flowings of the flesh. [[1:4|Basan languisheth|Infirmatus est Basan]], that is, all the power of the sinner will fail at the end of the world: for, being full of vices, he is inwardly disordered and confused, since he has not fulfilled that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 14:40|let all things be done decently and according to order|Omnia honeste et secundum ordinem fiant]] among you. Now Basan is interpreted *confusion*. [[1:4|and Carmel|Et Carmelus]], that is, one endowed only with a literal and carnal knowledge of circumcision: such as are the gross Jews, who follow the letter that killeth, not the spirit that quickeneth. Carmel is interpreted *knowledge of circumcision*. [[1:4|and the flower of Libanus fadeth away|Et flos Libani elanguit]], that is, all the greenness, beauty, comeliness and prosperity of the world shall waste away. Libanus is interpreted *whitening*: by which are understood here worldly hearts, flowering for a time, or making a show of holiness and adorning themselves outwardly with pretence. Of these it is sung: [[Ps 36:2|For they shall shortly wither away as grass, and as the green herbs shall quickly fall|Quoniam tanquam fœnum velociter arescent, et sicut olera herbarum cito decident]]. Hence in the book of Wisdom they confess: [[Wis 5:8|What hath pride profited us? or what advantage hath the boasting of riches brought us?|Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis?]] [[Wis 5:9|All those things are passed away like a shadow|Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra præteriens]]; [[Wis 5:13|we also being born, forthwith ceased to be|et nos nati, continuo desivimus esse]].

paras.t: Montes commoti sunt ab eo, et colles desolati sunt. Tunc enim complanabitur terra, montibus et collibus in planum redactis. Superbi quoque tunc humiliabuntur ac desolabuntur a Deo. Et contremuit terra a facie ejus: quoniam homines tunc arescent præ timore et exspectatione quæ supervenient universo orbi.
paras.en: [[1:5|The mountains tremble at him, and the hills are made desolate|Montes commoti sunt ab eo, et colles desolati sunt]]. For then the earth will be made level, the mountains and hills being brought down to a plain. The proud too will then be humbled and made desolate by God. [[1:5|and the earth hath quaked at his presence|Et contremuit terra a facie ejus]]: for men will then wither away [[Luke 21:26|for fear and expectation of what shall come upon the whole world|præ timore et exspectatione quæ supervenient universo orbi]].

paras.t: Ante faciem indignationis ejus quis stabit? id est, quis tolerare poterit iram Christi tunc indignantis? quasi dicat : Hoc pœnalissimum erit. Propter quod ait vir sanctus : Quis mihi tribuat ut in inferno protegas me, donec pertranseat furor tuus? Et Jeremias precatur : Corripe me, Domine, verumtamen non in furore, ne forte ad nihilum redigas me. Indignatio ejus effusa est ut ignis, id est, in die judicii horribilissime ac acerbissime effundetur, quando et ignis conflagrationis faciem mundi exuret, viventes in mundo occidet, et durante judicio inflammabit in circuitu inimicos Christi. Hinc scriptum est in Job : In diem perditionis servatur malus, et ad diem furoris ducetur, et de furore Omnipotentis bibet. Et petræ dissolutæ sunt ab eo, id est calore ignis illius, qui tunc omnia mixta corrumpet, quæ secundum se tota naturaliter corruptibilia sunt. Petra autem est quid mixtum, quoniam ex terra pura non fit lapis, secundum Avicennam.
paras.en: [[1:6|Who can stand before the face of his indignation?|Ante faciem indignationis ejus quis stabit?]] that is, who will be able to bear the wrath of Christ, indignant then? As if to say: This will be most grievous of all. Wherefore the holy man [Job] says: [[Job 14:13|Who will grant me this, that thou mayst protect me in hell|Quis mihi tribuat ut in inferno protegas me]], [[Job 14:13|till thy wrath pass|donec pertranseat furor tuus]]? And Jeremias prays: [[Jer 10:24|Correct me, O Lord, but yet|Corripe me, Domine, verumtamen]] [[Jer 10:24|not in thy fury, lest thou bring me to nothing|non in furore, ne forte ad nihilum redigas me]] [Denis's text leaves out the prophet's "with judgment"]. [[1:6|his indignation is poured out like fire|Indignatio ejus effusa est ut ignis]], that is, on the day of judgment it will be poured out most dreadfully and most bitterly, when the fire of the conflagration will burn up the face of the world, kill those living in the world, and, while the judgment lasts, burn up the enemies of Christ round about. Hence it is written in Job: [[Job 21:30|the wicked man is reserved to the day of destruction, and he shall be brought to the day of wrath|In diem perditionis servatur malus, et ad diem furoris ducetur]], [[Job 21:20|and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty|et de furore Omnipotentis bibet]]. [[1:6|and the rocks are melted by him|Et petræ dissolutæ sunt ab eo]], that is, by the heat of that fire, which will then corrupt all mixed bodies [*mixta*: bodies compounded of the elements], which in their whole selves are by nature corruptible. And a rock is a mixed body, since stone is not made of pure earth, according to Avicenna.

paras.t: Bonus est Dominus et confortans in die tribulationis. Electis enim erit tunc mitis, dulcis et confortativus. Et in diluvio prætereunte, id est tribulatione tunc abundante per modum diluvii et cito finem habentem, quoniam propter electos breviabitur tempus illud, consummationem faciet loci ejus, id est Ecclesiæ, tam quoad electos quam quoad reprobos. In electis enim tunc fiet consummatio, id est perfecta salvatio, et hæc est consummatio perfectiva; in reprobis vero fiet consummatio, id est perfecta damnatio, quæ est consummatio consumptiva. Quemadmodum nempe duplex est finis, scilicet finis perficiens et finis consumens (nam primo modo Deus est finis noster, secundo modo mors finis vocatur), sic duplex est consummatio. Inimicos ejus persequentur tenebræ : projicientur enim in tenebras exteriores cum angelis tenebrarum. Unde in libro Job dicitur : Antequam vadam ad terram tenebrosam et opertam mortis caligine, terram miseriæ et tenebrarum.
paras.en: [[1:7|The Lord is good, and giveth strength in the day of trouble|Bonus est Dominus et confortans in die tribulationis]]. For to the elect he will then be gentle, sweet and strengthening. [[1:8|But with a flood that passeth by|Et in diluvio prætereunte]], that is, with the tribulation then abounding after the manner of a flood and soon having an end, since for the sake of the elect that time will be shortened, [[1:8|he will make an utter end of the place thereof|consummationem faciet loci ejus]], that is, of the Church, as regards both the elect and the reprobate. For in the elect there will then be a consummation, that is, perfect salvation, and this is a perfecting consummation; but in the reprobate there will be a consummation, that is, perfect damnation, which is a consuming consummation [*consummatio*, here rendered "utter end", means both a bringing to completion and a consuming]. For just as an end is twofold, namely an end that perfects and an end that consumes (for in the first way God is our end, in the second way death is called an end), so consummation is twofold. [[1:8|and darkness shall pursue his enemies|Inimicos ejus persequentur tenebræ]]: for they will be cast into the exterior darkness with the angels of darkness. Hence it is said in the book of Job: [[Job 10:21|Before I go|Antequam vadam]] [[Job 10:21|to a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death|ad terram tenebrosam et opertam mortis caligine]], [[Job 10:22|A land of misery and darkness|terram miseriæ et tenebrarum]].

paras.t: Quid cogitatis contra Dominum, id est ea quæ displicent Deo, videlicet diu prosperari ac deliciari in sæculo isto? Consummationem ipse faciet, id est, cito finem imponet vestris deliciis cogitationibusque iniquis : quemadmodum ei qui dixerat, Anima mea, habes plura bona reposita in annos plurimos, requiesce, comede, bibe, epulare; Dominus ait : Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetunt a te; quæ autem parasti, cujus erunt?
paras.en: [[1:9|What do ye devise against the Lord|Quid cogitatis contra Dominum]], that is, the things that displease God, namely to prosper long and to live in delights in this world? [[1:9|he will make an utter end|Consummationem ipse faciet]], that is, he will soon put an end to your delights and wicked devisings: as to him who had said, [[Luke 12:19|Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years. Take thy rest: eat, drink, make good cheer|Anima mea, habes plura bona reposita in annos plurimos, requiesce, comede, bibe, epulare]], the Lord says: [[Luke 12:20|Thou fool, this night do they require thy soul of thee. And whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?|Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetunt a te; quæ autem parasti, cujus erunt?]]

paras.t: Et non consurget duplex tribulatio. Pro quo Septuaginta transtulerunt, Non vindicabit Dominus bis in id ipsum in tribulatione; Symmachus autem, Non sustinebunt impetum secundæ angustiæ; Theodotion, Non consurget secunda tribulatio. Circa hunc locum dicit Hieronymus, et habetur partim in Glossa : Si Deus legis videtur cruentus, rigidus et crudelis, quod genus humanum diluvio, Sodomitas igne et sulfure, Ægyptios mari, filios Israel in eremo interfecit, scitote eum ideo ad præsens reddidisse supplicia, ne in æternum puniret. Qui ergo puniti sunt, postea non punientur; alioqui mentitur Scriptura : quod nefas est dicere. Præterea dicit Hieronymus : Quærat hic aliquis, si fidelis deprehensus in adulterio decolletur, quid de eo postea fiet. Aut enim punietur, et falsa erit ista scriptura; aut non, et optandum erit ei nunc puniri, quatenus cruciatus evadat æternos. Ad quod (inquit) respondebimus, Deum ut omnium rerum, ita et suppliciorum scire mensuras, nec præveniri eum sententia hominis judicantis, et magnum peccatum magnis diuturnisque lui cruciatibus. Si autem punitus sit quis, sicut ille qui sabbato ligna collegerat, tales postea non puniri, quoniam levis culpa præsenti supplicio compensatur. Hæc recitando, non determinando, inserui. Solent tamen doctores asserere, quod Deus non vindicabit bis in id ipsum, dummodo una pœna sufficiens sit : alioqui quorumdam punitio hic inchoatur, et in inferis perpetuatur.
paras.en: [[1:9|there shall not rise a double affliction|Et non consurget duplex tribulatio]]. For this the Septuagint translated: The Lord will not take vengeance twice for the same thing in tribulation; Symmachus: They shall not endure the onset of a second distress; Theodotion: A second tribulation shall not rise. On this place Jerome says (and it is found in part in the Gloss): If the God of the Law seems bloody, harsh and cruel, because he slew the human race by the flood, the Sodomites by fire and brimstone, the Egyptians by the sea, and the children of Israel in the desert, know that he dealt out the punishments in the present for this reason, that he might not punish for ever. Those, then, who have been punished will not be punished afterwards; otherwise Scripture lies, which it is impious to say. Jerome further says: Someone may ask here, if a believer caught in adultery is beheaded, what will become of him afterwards. For either he will be punished, and then this scripture will be false; or not, and then it will be desirable for him to be punished now, so as to escape eternal torments. To this (he says) we shall answer that God knows the measures of punishments, as of all things, and is not forestalled by the sentence of a human judge, and that a great sin is atoned for by great and lasting torments; but if anyone has been punished, like him who had gathered sticks on the sabbath[[Num 15:32||]], such are not punished afterwards, since a light fault is paid for by the present punishment. These things I have put in by way of report, not of decision. The doctors, however, are wont to assert that God will not take vengeance twice for the same thing provided that one punishment is sufficient: otherwise the punishment of some begins here and is made perpetual in hell.

paras.t: Quæri potest, si vera sunt hæc, quomodo pro eodem peccato infligitur duplex pœna, videlicet damni et sensus. Dicendum, quod prædicta auctoritas loquitur de pœna sensus. Dicitur autem duplex pœna deberi peccato, propter duo quæ considerantur in eo : quorum unum est velut materiale, puta conversio mentis ad bonum caducum, ratione cujus infligitur pœna sensus; aliud est formale, videlicet aversio cordis a Deo, cui respondet pœna damni, utpote carentia divinæ visionis.
paras.en: It may be asked, if these things are true, how a twofold punishment is inflicted for the same sin, namely that of loss and that of sense [the pain of loss is the privation of the sight of God; the pain of sense, the torment that is felt]. The answer is that the authority cited speaks of the pain of sense. Now a twofold punishment is said to be due to sin because of two things that are considered in it: of which one is as it were material, namely the turning of the mind to a perishing good, by reason of which the pain of sense is inflicted; the other is formal, namely the turning of the heart away from God, to which the pain of loss answers, that is, the lack of the divine vision.

paras.t: Sicut spinæ se invicem complectuntur, ut simul comburantur, sic convivium eorum pariter potantium consumetur : id est, omnes epulationes et delectationes inanes carnalium, maxime hæreticorum, æternis suppliciis concludentur. De quibus ait Judas in sua Canonica : Hi sunt in epulis convivantes sine timore, semetipsos pascentes, nubes sine aqua : quibus procella tenebrarum conservata est usque in sempiternum.
paras.en: [[1:10|as thorns embrace one another|Sicut spinæ se invicem complectuntur]], so as to be burned together, [[1:10|so while they are feasting and drinking together, they shall be consumed|sic convivium eorum pariter potantium consumetur]]: that is, all the feastings and empty delights of carnal men, above all of heretics, will be shut up in eternal torments. Of whom Jude says in his Canonical Epistle: These are in their banquets, [[Jude 1:12|feasting together without fear, feeding themselves: clouds without water|convivantes sine timore, semetipsos pascentes, nubes sine aqua]], [[Jude 1:13|to whom the storm of darkness is reserved for ever|quibus procella tenebrarum conservata est usque in sempiternum]].

paras.t: Ex te, o Ecclesia, exibit cogitans contra Dominum malitiam, id est multitudo hæreticorum et aliorum transgressorum, qui contraria fidei cogitant atque efficiunt, quemadmodum ait Apostolus in Actibus : Ex vobis ipsis exsurgent viri loquentes perversa, ut abducant discipulos post se. De illis quoque scriptum est : Ex nobis prodierunt, sed non erant ex nobis.
paras.en: [[1:11|Out of thee|Ex te]], O Church, [[1:11|shall come forth one that imagineth evil against the Lord|exibit cogitans contra Dominum malitiam]], that is, the multitude of heretics and other transgressors, who devise and do things contrary to the faith; as the Apostle says in the Acts: [[Acts 20:30|of your own selves shall arise men speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them|Ex vobis ipsis exsurgent viri loquentes perversa, ut abducant discipulos post se]]. Of them too it is written: [[1 John 2:19|They went out from us but they were not of us|Ex nobis prodierunt, sed non erant ex nobis]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus : Si perfecti fuerint, et ita plures, etc., id est, quantumcumque multiplicent et confortentur iniqui, nihilo minus omnes facillime divina virtute pariter damnabuntur; eruntque tam molles seu impotentes ad resistendum, ut pilus ac lana ante novaculam, ideo attondendi dicuntur. Afflixi te, o Ecclesia electorum, quæ per ignem et aquam transisti, et non affligam te ultra post diem judicii : quia tunc Deus absterget omnem lacrimam ab oculis Sanctorum; et mors non erit ultra, nec ullus dolor.
paras.en: [[1:12|Thus saith the Lord: Though they were perfect: and many of them so|Hæc dicit Dominus : Si perfecti fuerint, et ita plures]], etc., that is, however much the wicked multiply and grow strong, nonetheless they will all together be condemned most easily by the divine power; and they will be as soft, or as powerless to resist, as hair and wool before the razor: that is why they are said to be shorn [*attondentur*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "cut off"]. [[1:12|I have afflicted thee|Afflixi te]], O Church of the elect, who hast passed through fire and water, [[1:12|and I will afflict thee no more|et non affligam te ultra]] after the day of judgment: for then [[Apoc 21:4|God shall wipe away all tears|Deus absterget omnem lacrimam]] from the eyes of the Saints; [[Apoc 21:4|and death shall be no more|et mors non erit ultra]], nor any sorrow.

paras.t: Et nunc conteram virgam ejus, id est tentationem diaboli persecutionemque mundi, de dorso tuo. Interdum enim dat Dominus servulis suis dulcia intervalla, ne sit pressura continua : imo sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita per Christum abundat et consolatio nostra. Et vincula tua, o prædestinate, dirumpam, a pœnis et culpis te eruendo.
paras.en: [[1:13|And now I will break in pieces his rod|Et nunc conteram virgam ejus]], that is, the temptation of the devil and the persecution of the world, from [[1:13|thy back|de dorso tuo]]. For at times the Lord gives his little servants sweet respites, lest the pressure be unbroken: nay, [[2 Cor 1:5|as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita per Christum abundat et consolatio nostra]]. [[1:13|and I will burst thy bonds|Et vincula tua]], O predestined one, [[1:13|asunder|dirumpam]], by delivering thee from punishments and from sins.

paras.t: Et præcipiet super te Dominus : id est, angelis sanctis in fine mundi mandabit contra ecclesiam reproborum, ut eos ad locum judicii deferant, atque in eos sententiam damnationis exsequi curent, quemadmodum ait Salvator : In consummatione sæculi exibunt angeli, et separabunt malos de medio justorum, et mittent eos in caminum ignis. Non seminabitur ex nomine tuo amplius, id est, semen operationis tuæ deficiet, nec alios falles ut filii tui dicantur. Finito enim judicio, ista cessabunt. Dies namque judicii non relinquet eis radicem, nec facient amplius fructum. De domo dei tui interficiam, id est, te exsistentem in adhæsione rerum creatarum, quas magis colis quam verum Deum (sicut quorumdam venter est deus), damnabo. Sculptile et conflatile ponam sepulcrum tuum, id est, inter vanitatis tuæ simulacra sopore peccati deficies, et profundo obstinationis clauderis, ita ut absorbeat te profundum, claudatque super te puteus os suum; quia inhonoratus es, id est propter peccata vilis et tali tumulo dignus effectus. Qui enim contemnunt Dominum, erunt ignobiles, secundum quod ait primo Regum.
paras.en: [[1:14|And the Lord will give a commandment concerning thee|Et præcipiet super te Dominus]]: that is, at the end of the world he will give command to the holy angels against the church of the reprobate, that they bring them to the place of judgment and see that the sentence of damnation is carried out upon them; as the Saviour says: [[Matt 13:49|at the end of the world. The angels shall go out, and shall separate the wicked from among the just|In consummatione sæculi exibunt angeli, et separabunt malos de medio justorum]], [[Matt 13:50|And shall cast them into the furnace of fire|et mittent eos in caminum ignis]]. [[1:14|no more of thy name shall be sown|Non seminabitur ex nomine tuo amplius]], that is, the seed of thy working shall fail, nor shalt thou deceive others so that they be called thy children. For when the judgment is finished, these things will cease; for the day of judgment will leave them no root, nor will they bear fruit any more. [[1:14|out of the house of thy God|De domo dei tui]] [[1:14|I will destroy|interficiam]], that is, I will condemn thee who abidest in clinging to created things, which thou worshippest more than the true God (as some have their belly for their god[[Phil 3:19||]]). [[1:14|the graven and molten thing|Sculptile et conflatile]] [[1:14|I will make it thy grave|ponam sepulcrum tuum]], that is, among the idols of thy vanity thou shalt waste away in the sleep of sin, and shalt be shut in the deep of obstinacy, so that the deep swallow thee up and the pit shut its mouth upon thee[[Ps 68:16||]]; [[1:14|for thou art disgraced|quia inhonoratus es]], that is, made vile by sins and worthy of such a tomb. For they that despise the Lord shall be ignoble[[1 Kings 2:30||]], as it says in the first book of Kings.

paras.t: Ecce super montes, id est in altis locis Ecclesiæ, vel in sublimitate virtutum et apice contemplationum, sunt pedes evangelizantis et annuntiantis pacem, id est doctorum et prædicatorum bonorum, qui fidelium corda contra tentationes et persecutiones confortant, victoriamque in nomine Christi promittunt, dicentes illud Apostoli : Deus conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter. Potest quoque allegorice exponi de Christo, et mystice de Præcursore. Unde ad litteram scriptum est in Isaia : Super montem excelsum ascende, tu qui evangelizas Sion; et, Quam pulchri super montes pedes annuntiantium pacem, etc.! Celebra, Juda, id est, Ecclesia ore et corde confitens Deo, festivitates tuas, id est, divinis jugiter atque celebriter esto intenta; et redde vota tua, id est, gratiarum actiones et promissa sanctaque desideria : juxta illud, In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, quæ reddam laudationes tibi; et item, Vota mea Domino reddam in conspectu omnis populi ejus.
paras.en: [[1:15|Behold upon the mountains|Ecce super montes]], that is, in the high places of the Church, or in the height of the virtues and the summit of contemplation, are [[1:15|the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, and that preacheth peace|pedes evangelizantis et annuntiantis pacem]], that is, of good doctors and preachers, who strengthen the hearts of the faithful against temptations and persecutions and promise victory in the name of Christ, saying that word of the Apostle: God will [[Rom 16:20|crush Satan under your feet speedily|conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter]]. It can also be expounded allegorically of Christ, and mystically of the Forerunner. Hence it is written according to the letter in Isaias: [[Is 40:9|Get thee up upon a high mountain, thou that bringest good tidings to Sion|Super montem excelsum ascende, tu qui evangelizas Sion]]; and: [[Is 52:7|How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, and that preacheth peace|Quam pulchri super montes pedes annuntiantium pacem]], etc.! [[1:15|O Juda, keep|Celebra, Juda]], that is, O Church, confessing to God with mouth and heart [Juda is interpreted *confession*], [[1:15|thy festivals|festivitates tuas]], that is, be ever and solemnly intent on divine things; [[1:15|and pay thy vows|et redde vota tua]], that is, thanksgivings, promises and holy desires: according to that word, [[Ps 55:12|In me, O God, are vows to thee, which I will pay, praises to thee|In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, quæ reddam laudationes tibi]]; and again, [[Ps 115:9|I will pay my vows to the Lord in the sight of all his people|Vota mea Domino reddam in conspectu omnis populi ejus]] [the margin gives Ps. cxv, 18, the Hebrew numbering (Ps 116:18); in the Vulgate it is Ps 115:9].

paras.t: Quia non adjiciet ultra ut pertranseat in te Belial, id est diabolus, qui factus est ut nullum timeret, consecutive, non directe : de quo loquitur Paulus : Quæ conventio Christi ad Belial? Universus interiit, id est, victus atque exclusus est. Christus nempe fortem armatum ligavit, et vasa ejus diripuit. Istud tamen post diem judicii plene complebitur : nam quamdiu durat præsens vita, durat tentatio, quum militia sit vita hominis super terram. Nunc quoque Belial non transit in nobis, quamdiu non consentimus, sed implemus illud Apostoli : Nolite locum dare diabolo; et illud Jacobi, Resistite diabolo, et fugiet a vobis. Aliqui etiam adstruunt, quod diabolus semel victus ab aliquo, non amplius tentat eumdem. Quod S. Thomas intelligendum affirmat, quoad aliquod tempus : quemadmodum scriptum est in Luca de Christo, quod consummata omni tentatione, diabolus recessit ab eo usque ad tempus.
paras.en: [[1:15|for Belial shall no more pass through thee again|Quia non adjiciet ultra ut pertranseat in te Belial]], that is, the devil, [[Job 41:24|who was made to fear no one|qui factus est ut nullum timeret]] (consequently, not directly [that is, fearlessness followed from the nature he was given, but was not the purpose of his making]), of whom Paul speaks: [[2 Cor 6:15|what concord hath Christ with Belial?|Quæ conventio Christi ad Belial?]] [[1:15|he is utterly cut off|Universus interiit]], that is, he has been conquered and shut out. For Christ bound the strong man armed and plundered his goods[[Matt 12:29||]] ["the strong man armed" is Luke's wording, Luke 11:21]. Yet this will be fully accomplished only after the day of judgment: for as long as the present life lasts, temptation lasts, since the [[Job 7:1|life of man upon earth is a warfare|militia sit vita hominis super terram]]. Even now Belial does not pass through us so long as we do not consent, but fulfil that word of the Apostle: [[Eph 4:27|Give not place to the devil|Nolite locum dare diabolo]]; and that of James: [[Jas 4:7|resist the devil: and he will fly from you|Resistite diabolo, et fugiet a vobis]]. Some also maintain that the devil, once conquered by someone, does not tempt the same person any more. This St. Thomas declares is to be understood as for some time: as it is written in Luke of Christ, that [[Luke 4:13|all the temptation being ended, the devil departed from him for a time|consummata omni tentatione, diabolus recessit ab eo usque ad tempus]].
